title: ついに — “finally / in the end”
summary: ついに is an adverb that shows a result reached after a long time or much effort: “finally.” With a positive verb it conveys a long-awaited result. With a negative verb it means “in the end ... did not happen.”

patterns.form: ついに ＋ 動詞（過去形）
patterns.gloss: ついに + verb in the past (ついに完成した)

patterns.form: ついに ＋ 動詞ない形（過去）
patterns.gloss: ついに + negative past (ついに来なかった): in the end, it didn't happen

body.p: After a long process, a result arrives: 三年かかって、ついに小説が完成した. It usually carries a sense of achievement or relief. The result is something expected or hoped for.
With a negative verb it says something never happened despite waiting: 待ち続けたが、返事はついに来なかった. It carries disappointment.

body.h: Difference from やっと / とうとう
body.p: やっと stresses the difficulty or effort until the result. とうとう and ついに are very close and focus on the final arrival after a long time. ついに is a little more formal.

examples.ja: 三年（さんねん）かかって、ついに小説（しょうせつ）が完成（かんせい）した。
examples.romaji: Sannen kakatte, tsui ni shōsetsu ga kansei shita.
examples.tr: After three years, the novel was finally completed.

examples.ja: 長年（ながねん）の努力（どりょく）が実（みの）り、ついに夢（ゆめ）がかなった。
examples.romaji: Naganen no doryoku ga minori, tsui ni yume ga kanatta.
examples.tr: My years of effort paid off, and my dream finally came true.

examples.ja: 待（ま）ち続（つづ）けたが、返事（へんじ）はついに来（こ）なかった。
examples.romaji: Machitsuzuketa ga, henji wa tsui ni konakatta.
examples.tr: I kept waiting, but in the end the reply never came.
examples.note: A negative verb: it never happened.

pitfalls: Do not confuse it with つい (unintentionally). ついに has the long-wait meaning.
It is used for results that have already happened. For a future plan, use やっと〜できそうだ or そろそろ.
